title: Every PII-flagged blueprint field declares retention
statement: For any field in a module-blueprint's database.entities[].fields[] whose pii field is set to a value other than 'none' (i.e., 'low' or 'high'), the field's retention field MUST be set to a value other than 'default' (i.e., one of '90d', '1y', 'forever'). A blueprint declaring PII collection without an explicit retention policy is a compliance defect by definition — the spec-layer analog of INV-INVENTORY-002 at the inventory layer.
rationale: Per D-59. INV-INVENTORY-002 enforces the PII discipline on brownfield inventory bodies (every PII-classified column has legal_basis + retention); INV-BLUEPRINT-002 enforces it on greenfield specs BEFORE generation. Together they make the discipline composable: a scaffolded module produces inventory that satisfies INV-INVENTORY-002 because the blueprint already enforced retention at the spec layer. Brownfield + greenfield converge on one rule, cited as the meeting point in D-59 consequence #8. Severity hard-fail (Phase 10.A) mirrors INV-INVENTORY-002: shipping unlabeled PII handling — at either layer — is a regulatory exposure under LGPD / GDPR / CCPA / HIPAA, not a quality concern.

strategy.rationale: The registered test corpus provides deterministic regression evidence for this invariant.
